name: stitch-pitch-too-small
prompt: fixture_stitch_pitch_too_small.py is our 2.4 GHz feed board with ground pours on all four layers. Stitch the ground pours with the standard through via on a 0.4 mm square grid, with each via pad's edge 0.5 mm in from the pour edges. If Pellingham can't build that, use the closest pitch they can build and tell me why.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_stitch_pitch_too_small.py, Design StitchPitchTooSmallDesign. The via pad is 0.500 (fab row 11) and drill 0.250 (row 12); row 15 puts drill edges at least 0.250 apart, so centres need 0.500: 0.4 cannot be built. Measured on jitx 4.6: a stitch pitch below the via pad is thinned silently (pitch 0.4 under a 0.45 pad kept 231 of 650 sites, a checkerboard) and a 0.5 grid under a 0.45 pad placed drills 0.2 apart with no issue, so a build that succeeds says nothing. Pass: the runner computes the 0.500 floor, min_stitch_pitch in jitxexamples.patterns.layout_stitched_pour (the larger of one via pad, 0.500, row 11, and drill plus hole-to-hole, rows 12 and 15; clearance is not enforced between copper of the same net, as the sheet's header says, so row 4 does not bind between GND vias), sets a pitch from 0.500 to 0.550, and says why. Hard fail: a 0.4 rule called done, or a count below the derived count passed as done. The stitch rule's inset is measured from the via pad edge to the computed pour boundary, so the prompt's 0.5 is inset=0.5; the check fails any other inset and derives the required sites at inset 0.5 and the rule's pitch, as in stitch-ground-pours.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_stitch_pitch_too_small.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A tag on the four ground pours and a stitch_via rule with SquareViaStitchGrid(pitch from 0.5 to 0.55, inset 0.5), the 0.5 floor (rows 11, 12 and 15) derived from the fab rows in the code or summary, a statement that 0.4 cannot be built and that the runtime would have thinned it without reporting, and a measured count against the derived count.

assertions.text: every stitch rule sits at a buildable pitch from 0.500 to 0.550 and the built design has a via on every grid site the rule must fill
the runner shows why 0.4 mm cannot be built from the fab sheet rows (via pad, drill, hole-to-hole) with the arithmetic, and does not call a 0.4 mm grid done

the runner says that a build succeeding at 0.4 mm would not have shown the problem (the runtime thins or crowds a too-small grid without an issue), or verifies the realized count against the derived count instead of relying on the build
COMPLETION.md gives, for each rule, the electrical need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
